hypothesis: A no-propagator onset hypernetwork trained against the correctly loaded r5b parent can learn a future-residual initialization from train episodes, whereas all prior r5b hypernetwork runs were trained against the 35-times amplified parent correction.
mechanism: Offline supervised meta-learning transfers cross-record residual structure into a shared conditioner and residual head; online adaptation updates only 32 latent shifts and one gate from two onset frames.
cross_domain_basis: amortized meta-learning plus low-dimensional test-time optimization, analogous to learned system identification
primary_metric: best_epoch_mean_loss on the identical 12 train episodes
failure_signal: Every learning rate reduces the paired train objective by less than 1 percent or becomes nonfinite.
selection_rule: Choose the finite checkpoint with the lowest best_epoch_mean_loss; ties choose the lower learning rate.
next_gate: The selected checkpoint must improve future-field error on group-disjoint train episodes excluded from these 12 meta-training groups before validation can be reopened.
rollback: Preserve every prior r5b, CPADC, A3, B2-H, and Helmholtz checkpoint; reject all four isolated outputs if the gate fails.
